patterns.description: Un conjunto de cartas co-ocurre alrededor del tema de visibilidad orgánica en Gumroad Discover: SC-R1-055, SC-R1-062, SC-R1-049, SC-R1-073 y SC-R1-069 se concentran en el mismo territorio de descubrimiento de productos desde múltiples fuentes.

signal_summaries.SC-R1-055: Blog: Gumroad will not promote through Discover until seller earns first $10
signal_summaries.SC-R1-062: Seller forum: 26 products with zero Discover views; all views from own traffic; Discover only shows products after first sale
signal_summaries.SC-R1-049: Blog: seller with 35 products receiving zero organic traffic
signal_summaries.SC-R1-073: Help center: products listed on Discover once unspecified eligibility criteria satisfied and category selected
signal_summaries.SC-R1-069: Help center: adding category and tags helps Gumroad show products on Discover

patterns.routing_rationale: Five cards from four distinct source URLs (najfywrites.substack.com, indiehackers.com, medium.com/never-stop-writing, help.gumroad.com/article/79, help.gumroad.com/article/123) co-occur around the same topic of Gumroad Discover organic visibility. DT question test: does resolving the relationship between these cards change a design decision? Yes — a seller deciding whether to rely on Gumroad Discover for organic traffic vs investing in external marketing channels would make a different decision depending on whether Discover reliably delivers organic views or requires a prior first-sale threshold. The cluster spans official documentation and independent seller reports.

components.label: Official platform documentation on Discover eligibility
components.summary: Two help center cards document Discover eligibility criteria (category selection, tags, unspecified eligibility) without specifying first-sale threshold

components.label: Seller-reported experience of Discover visibility
components.summary: Three cards from blog and forum sources document zero organic Discover traffic before first sale, with 26-35 products listed across two independent sellers

patterns.description: Un conjunto de cartas co-ocurre alrededor del tema de tarifas y estructura de costos de Gumroad: SC-R1-005, SC-R1-006, SC-R1-007, SC-R1-032, SC-R1-035, SC-R1-036, SC-R1-038 y SC-R1-044 se concentran en la misma temática de costos desde múltiples fuentes distintas.

signal_summaries.SC-R1-005: Pricing page: 10% + $0.50 per transaction for standard sales
signal_summaries.SC-R1-032: Help center: 10% flat fee, $0 to start
signal_summaries.SC-R1-035: Help center fees article: 10% flat fee for web sales
signal_summaries.SC-R1-036: Fees article: 40% total for mobile app sales
signal_summaries.SC-R1-038: Discover help: 40% fee for in-app sales
signal_summaries.SC-R1-044: Blog: observed effective fee range 8%-20% depending on price and country

patterns.routing_rationale: Eight cards from five distinct source URLs (gumroad.com/pricing, help.gumroad.com/article/303, help.gumroad.com/article/66, help.gumroad.com/article/79, medium.com) co-occur around the topic of Gumroad fee structure. DT question test: does resolving the relationship between these cards change a design decision? Yes — a seller deciding which sales channel to optimize (direct web link vs Discover vs mobile app) would make different decisions depending on which fee rate applies. The co-occurrence cluster spans three distinct fee tiers across official and seller sources, with units declared as non-normalized (percentage-only vs percentage-plus-fixed-charge).

components.label: Official documentation on fee tiers by channel
components.summary: Seven cards from official Gumroad sources document fee rates across channels: 10%-10%+$0.50 standard, 30% Discover web, 40% mobile app

components.label: Seller-observed effective fee range
components.summary: One blog card documents observed effective fee range of 8%-20% depending on price and country, without specifying the mechanism

patterns.description: Un conjunto de cartas co-ocurre alrededor del tema de control de la plataforma sobre vendedores y sus productos: SC-R1-014, SC-R1-015, SC-R1-016, SC-R1-017, SC-R1-018 y SC-R1-023 se concentran en la estructura contractual de discreción exclusiva de Gumroad.

signal_summaries.SC-R1-014: Policy page: prohibited items changes occur abruptly without notice, take effect immediately
signal_summaries.SC-R1-015: ToS: Gumroad acts as non-exclusive reseller of seller digital products at its discretion
signal_summaries.SC-R1-016: ToS: Gumroad has sole discretion to determine and change eligible product categories at any time; sellers cannot invoice buyers directly
signal_summaries.SC-R1-017: ToS: Gumroad fee automatically deducted; settlement schedule subject to change at Gumroad's discretion
signal_summaries.SC-R1-018: ToS: Gumroad handles refunds/chargebacks at sole discretion; sellers must reimburse Gumroad
signal_summaries.SC-R1-023: ToS: disputes must be individual not class action; right to jury trial waived; California law governs

patterns.routing_rationale: Six cards from two distinct source URLs (gumroad.com/prohibited and gumroad.com/terms) co-occur around the topic of platform-side control mechanisms. DT question test: does resolving the relationship between these cards change a design decision? Yes — a seller deciding whether to build a business dependent on Gumroad would make a different decision knowing the extent of unilateral discretion the platform retains over product eligibility, fee schedules, refunds, and dispute resolution. The cluster spans policy page and Terms of Service documents, representing multiple distinct mechanisms of platform control.

components.label: Policy mechanisms granting Gumroad unilateral discretion
components.summary: Five cards document Gumroad's sole discretion over: prohibited item policy changes, eligible product categories, reseller status, fee structures, and refund/chargeback handling

components.label: Legal/dispute mechanisms limiting seller recourse
components.summary: One card documents mandatory individual arbitration, waiver of jury trial right, and California law jurisdiction

patterns.description: Un conjunto de cartas co-ocurre alrededor del tema de resultados de ingresos de vendedores en Gumroad: SC-R1-050, SC-R1-060, SC-R1-054, SC-R1-039, SC-R1-056, SC-R1-051 y SC-R1-052 se distribuyen desde múltiples fuentes independientes reportando cifras de ventas.

signal_summaries.SC-R1-050: Blog: seller earned $61,411 in 2025, ranked #238 among all creators
signal_summaries.SC-R1-054: Blog: seller reported $65.15 in 4 hours and described $50-$200 daily organic revenue
signal_summaries.SC-R1-039: Blog: $3,271 in first 6 months from POD experiments
signal_summaries.SC-R1-056: Blog: $139.96 total in 3 years on Gumroad
signal_summaries.SC-R1-051: Blog: ~$21 in first week of selling
signal_summaries.SC-R1-052: Blog: seller announced sharing dashboard data for 50+ products including sales and failures

patterns.routing_rationale: Seven cards from seven distinct blog source URLs co-occur around seller income reporting. However, this is frequency clustering: many cards report different seller income figures. The DT question test fails here — these cards do not generate a question whose resolution would change a design decision about the platform itself. They are individual seller outcome reports that vary widely, representing the distribution of outcomes but not documenting a mechanism or friction between them. The asymmetric outcome distribution is captured in ASYM-001; this cluster here is pure frequency of income reports from the same platform.

components.label: High-outcome seller reports
components.summary: Three cards with seller-reported outcomes in the thousands to tens of thousands of dollars

components.label: Low-outcome seller reports
components.summary: Four cards with seller-reported outcomes from $21 to $3,271 over varying time periods

patterns.description: Un conjunto de cartas co-ocurre alrededor del tema de la estructura de pago y payout de vendedores en Gumroad: SC-R1-011, SC-R1-017, SC-R1-019, SC-R1-021, SC-R1-024, SC-R1-025, SC-R1-026, SC-R1-027, SC-R1-028, SC-R1-030 se concentran en el mecanismo de pago y retención de fondos desde múltiples fuentes.

signal_summaries.SC-R1-011: Pricing page: payout method (direct deposit or PayPal) varies by country
signal_summaries.SC-R1-017: ToS: Gumroad fee deducted automatically; settlement schedule subject to change at Gumroad's discretion
signal_summaries.SC-R1-019: ToS: all transactions settle in USD regardless of listed currency; exchange rates not guaranteed
signal_summaries.SC-R1-021: ToS: Gumroad uses Stripe and PayPal for payment processing
signal_summaries.SC-R1-024: Help center: if direct deposit and PayPal both unavailable, there is no way to pay the seller
signal_summaries.SC-R1-025: Help center: PayPal payouts in USD; Payoneer, Wise, check, wire not supported
signal_summaries.SC-R1-026: Help center: sale amounts sit in Gumroad balance for at least 7 days before payout; schedule not customizable
signal_summaries.SC-R1-027: Help center: 160+ countries can accept payments; payout method depends on country
signal_summaries.SC-R1-028: Help center: no payout if PayPal not supported in country; Payoneer, wire, bitcoin unavailable
signal_summaries.SC-R1-030: Help center: Gumroad uses Stripe for all credit card payments and bank payouts; subject to Stripe policies

patterns.routing_rationale: Ten cards from five distinct source URLs (gumroad.com/pricing, gumroad.com/terms, help.gumroad.com/article/13, help.gumroad.com/article/152, help.gumroad.com/article/260) co-occur around the topic of seller payment structure and payout mechanics. DT question test: does resolving the relationship between these cards change a design decision? Yes — a seller deciding whether to build on Gumroad as their primary sales channel would make a different decision knowing: (a) payout schedule is fixed and not customizable, (b) all settlements are in USD regardless of listing currency with unguaranteed exchange rates, (c) payout availability is geographically constrained, and (d) Stripe and PayPal policies apply. The cluster spans terms, pricing page, and help center documentation.

components.label: Settlement and currency mechanics
components.summary: Three cards document settlement timing (7-day hold minimum, non-customizable), USD-only settlement regardless of listing currency, and discretionary schedule changes

components.label: Geographic payout availability and third-party dependencies
components.summary: Seven cards document payout method dependency on seller country, Stripe and PayPal as the only third-party processors, geographic constraints on payout availability, and exclusion of alternative payout services
